Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 3a) demonstrates a right-sided pneumothorax where the visceral pleura has separated from the parietal pleura, causing the azygos lobe to shift laterally away from the mediastinum. This separation creates an "empty" appearance of the azygos fissure with air surrounding it, and the characteristic teardrop-shaped opacity of the azygos vein is no longer visible at its normal caudal termination due to the displacement and collapse.
